```{r hs_family_detection_heatmap, fig.width=13, fig.height=13}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7C: FAMILY DETECTION FREQUENCY BY HOST GROUP
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: how consistently each Family occurs within a host group.
#
# Detection means at least one retained ASV from that Family has reads
# greater than zero. The percentage is detected samples divided by ALL
# samples in the host group, including nondetections.
#
# Show every represented Family, not only the Top N composition set.
# Unassigned family means any unresolved ASV was detected; it is not one
# known shared taxon. A 100% value in an n=1 group represents one sample.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE DETECTION FREQUENCIES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
family_detection_frequency <- sample_family_asvs %>%
  group_by(tentative_species_id, Family_plot) %>%
  summarise(
    detected_samples = sum(number_of_asvs > 0),
    group_samples = n(),
    detection_percent = 100 * mean(number_of_asvs > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Keep the named-Family ranking from the composition plot, followed by
# Unassigned family when present. Split long lists into blocks of 40
# for readable labels; all blocks use the same host order and scale.
full_family_order <- c(
  family_ranking$Family_plot,
  intersect("Unassigned family", sample_family_asvs$Family_plot)
)

family_detection_blocks <- split(
  seq_along(full_family_order),
  ceiling(seq_along(full_family_order) / 40)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
for (family_indices in family_detection_blocks) {

  families_here <- full_family_order[family_indices]

  family_detection_plot_data <- family_detection_frequency %>%
    filter(Family_plot %in% families_here) %>%
    mutate(
      Family_plot = factor(Family_plot, levels = rev(families_here))
    )

  family_detection_plot <- ggplot(
    family_detection_plot_data,
    aes(
      x = tentative_species_id,
      y = Family_plot,
      fill = detection_percent
    )
  ) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = host_levels,
      labels = host_labels,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      colors = c("#FAFAFA", "#D1E5F0", "#67A9CF", "#2166AC", "#053061"),
      limits = c(0, 100),
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
      labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Family detection frequency by host group",
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Family categories ", min(family_indices), "-", max(family_indices),
        " of ", length(full_family_order)
      ),
      x = "Tentative host-spider species",
      y = "Family",
      fill = "Samples detected",
      caption = paste(
        "Percentages use all samples in each host group, including nondetections.",
        "Small groups provide limited evidence about typical occurrence; nondetection is not proof of absence.",
        sep = "\n"
      )
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
    )

  print(family_detection_plot)
}
```


```{r hs_family_upset, fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7D: NAMED-FAMILY SHARING AMONG HOST GROUPS
# ============================================================
#
# Exploratory figure: exact combinations of host groups sharing families.
#
# A Family belongs to a host-group set when at least one sample in
# that group has a positive detection. Filled dots in a column show
# the groups in one exact combination; unmarked groups are excluded.
# The upper bar counts families with exactly that combination.
# Left bars count all named families detected in each host group.
#
# Use all named families, not just the Top N display categories.
# Omit Unassigned family only from this overlap calculation because
# unresolved ASVs do not form one known shared taxon. Those ASVs remain
# in the other analyses. Shared Family labels need not mean shared
# species or ASVs. Group-only detections do not establish specificity.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# BUILD HOST-GROUP PRESENCE SETS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
family_host_presence <- family_detection_frequency %>%
  filter(Family_plot != "Unassigned family") %>%
  transmute(
    Family_plot,
    tentative_species_id,
    present = detected_samples > 0
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = tentative_species_id,
    values_from = present,
    values_fill = FALSE
  ) %>%
  select(Family_plot, all_of(host_levels))

presence_matrix <- family_host_presence %>%
  select(-Family_plot) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Each binary pattern identifies one exact combination of host groups.
# Families are counted once; intersection counts sum to all named families.
family_patterns <- apply(
  presence_matrix,
  1,
  function(x) paste(as.integer(x), collapse = "")
)

upset_intersections <- tibble(
  Family_plot = family_host_presence$Family_plot,
  pattern = family_patterns
) %>%
  group_by(pattern) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_families = n(),
    families = paste(sort(Family_plot), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(number_of_families), pattern) %>%
  mutate(intersection_id = row_number())

upset_membership <- do.call(
  rbind,
  strsplit(upset_intersections$pattern, "")
) == "1"

upset_set_sizes <- tibble(
  tentative_species_id = host_levels,
  host_position = rev(seq_along(host_levels)),
  number_of_families = as.numeric(colSums(presence_matrix))
)

# Show every observed combination in consecutive blocks of at most 20.
# Host labels, sample sizes and count scales stay the same in every block.
upset_blocks <- split(
  seq_len(nrow(upset_intersections)),
  ceiling(seq_len(nrow(upset_intersections)) / 20)
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
for (intersection_indices in upset_blocks) {

  upset_bar_data <- upset_intersections[intersection_indices, ] %>%
    mutate(column_position = row_number())

  upset_matrix_data <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    column_position = seq_along(intersection_indices),
    host_index = seq_along(host_levels)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      host_position = length(host_levels) + 1 - host_index,
      present = upset_membership[
        cbind(intersection_indices[column_position], host_index)
      ]
    )

  upset_lines <- upset_matrix_data %>%
    filter(present) %>%
    group_by(column_position) %>%
    summarise(
      first_host = min(host_position),
      last_host = max(host_position),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Upper bars align with the exact-combination columns below.
  upset_bar_plot <- ggplot(
    upset_bar_data,
    aes(x = column_position, y = number_of_families)
  ) +
    geom_col(fill = "#257C9D", width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = number_of_families), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, nrow(upset_bar_data) + 0.5),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0),
      breaks = NULL
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, max(upset_intersections$number_of_families) * 1.2),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Named families") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())

  # The left bars show total named-Family detections for each host set.
  upset_set_plot <- ggplot(
    upset_set_sizes,
    aes(x = number_of_families, y = host_position)
  ) +
    geom_col(
      aes(fill = tentative_species_id),
      orientation = "y",
      width = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_text(aes(label = number_of_families), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = host_colors) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)),
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 3)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, length(host_levels) + 0.5),
      breaks = rev(seq_along(host_levels)),
      labels = unname(host_labels),
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Named families detected", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10)
    )

  # Pale dots are unmarked groups; dark connected dots form one combination.
  upset_matrix_plot <- ggplot(
    upset_matrix_data,
    aes(x = column_position, y = host_position)
  ) +
    geom_point(color = "grey85", size = 2.4) +
    geom_segment(
      data = upset_lines,
      aes(
        x = column_position,
        xend = column_position,
        y = first_host,
        yend = last_host
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.6
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = upset_matrix_data %>% filter(present),
      color = "#172C3C",
      size = 2.7
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, nrow(upset_bar_data) + 0.5),
      breaks = upset_bar_data$column_position,
      labels = upset_bar_data$intersection_id,
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0.5, length(host_levels) + 0.5),
      breaks = seq_along(host_levels),
      labels = NULL,
      expand = expansion(mult = 0)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Observed combination", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

  # Align the three ggplot panels using grid, which is included with R.
  # Shared widths align upper bars with dots; shared heights align host rows.
  bar_grob <- ggplotGrob(upset_bar_plot)
  set_grob <- ggplotGrob(upset_set_plot)
  matrix_grob <- ggplotGrob(upset_matrix_plot)
  shared_widths <- grid::unit.pmax(bar_grob$widths, matrix_grob$widths)
  bar_grob$widths <- shared_widths
  matrix_grob$widths <- shared_widths
  shared_heights <- grid::unit.pmax(set_grob$heights, matrix_grob$heights)
  set_grob$heights <- shared_heights
  matrix_grob$heights <- shared_heights

  grid::grid.newpage()
  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(
    layout = grid::grid.layout(
      nrow = 4,
      ncol = 2,
      widths = grid::unit(c(5.5, 8.5), "null"),
      heights = grid::unit(c(0.65, 2.0, 4.5, 0.65), "null")
    )
  ))

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1, layout.pos.col = 1:2))
  grid::grid.text(
    "Observed Family sharing across host groups",
    y = 0.75,
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 15, fontface = "bold")
  )
  grid::grid.text(
    paste0(
      "Combinations ", min(intersection_indices), "-", max(intersection_indices),
      " of ", nrow(upset_intersections), "; all named families included"
    ),
    y = 0.22,
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11)
  )
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 2, layout.pos.col = 2))
  grid::grid.draw(bar_grob)
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 3, layout.pos.col = 1))
  grid::grid.draw(set_grob)
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 3, layout.pos.col = 2))
  grid::grid.draw(matrix_grob)
  grid::popViewport()

  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 4, layout.pos.col = 1:2))
  grid::grid.text(
    paste(
      "Each column is an exact observed host-group combination; the bar counts named families.",
      "Sampling is unequal. Group-only detections do not establish host specificity.",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 10)
  )
  grid::popViewport(2)
}
```


#### Spider detections in individual webs

```{r hs_spider_web_list, results='asis'}
# ============================================================
# SPIDER DETECTIONS IN INDIVIDUAL WEB SAMPLES
# ============================================================
#
# Follow-up to the Family summaries: which spiders were detected
# in each web, and how many identified spider genera were recovered?
#
# Reuse the final long table. Select positive-read Araneae records
# for this descriptive summary only; do not change the analysis
# dataset, community matrix, QC thresholds or downstream tests.
# Host identity comes from metadata. Detected spider taxa come from
# ASV taxonomy and include potential host-spider DNA.
#
# Count each identified genus once per web, regardless of how many
# ASVs represent it. Family and Order assignments remain visible
# but are not counted as additional identified genera. Read and ASV
# counts are sequencing support, not numbers of individual spiders.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PREPARE SPIDER TAXON LABELS AT THE EXISTING CONFIDENCE LEVELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
clean_spider_taxon <- function(x) {
  x <- str_squish(as.character(x))
  x[str_to_lower(x) %in% c(
    "", "na", "nan", "n/a", "null", "unknown", "unidentified",
    "unassigned", "unclassified"
  )] <- NA_character_
  x
}

spider_web_detections <- mco_HS_plot_data %>%
  filter(Order == "Araneae", reads > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    spider_species = clean_spider_taxon(Species),
    spider_genus = clean_spider_taxon(Genus),
    spider_family = clean_spider_taxon(Family),
    spider_assignment_rank = case_when(
      !is.na(spider_species) &
        !str_detect(
          spider_species,
          regex(
            "\\b(sp|spp|cf|aff|uncultured|unidentified|unclassified)\\b",
            ignore_case = TRUE
          )
        ) ~ "Species",
      !is.na(spider_genus) ~ "Genus",
      !is.na(spider_family) ~ "Family",
      TRUE ~ "Order"
    ),
    spider_taxon = case_when(
      spider_assignment_rank == "Species" ~ spider_species,
      spider_assignment_rank == "Genus" ~ paste(spider_genus, "sp. [genus]"),
      spider_assignment_rank == "Family" ~ paste(spider_family, "[family]"),
      TRUE ~ "Unassigned Araneae [order]"
    )
  )

# One row per spider assignment label in each web; merge supporting ASVs.
spider_web_taxa <- spider_web_detections %>%
  group_by(sample_id, spider_taxon, spider_assignment_rank) %>%
  summarise(
    spider_family = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(spider_family))), collapse = "; "),
    spider_asvs = n_distinct(query),
    spider_reads = sum(reads),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Use the existing host order and natural sample-ID order within hosts.
spider_web_order <- analysis_sample_metadata %>%
  arrange(
    tentative_species_id,
    match(sample_id, str_sort(sample_id, numeric = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  pull(sample_id)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# COUNT IDENTIFIED GENERA AND RETAIN ALL WEB SAMPLES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
spider_web_summary <- spider_web_detections %>%
  mutate(
    genus_for_count = spider_genus
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    number_of_spider_genera = n_distinct(
      genus_for_count, na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    spider_genus_list = if (any(!is.na(genus_for_count))) {
      paste(
        sort(unique(na.omit(genus_for_count))),
        collapse = "; "
      )
    } else {
      "No genus-level assignment"
    },
    unresolved_spider_asvs = n_distinct(
      query[is.na(genus_for_count)]
    ),
    number_of_spider_asvs = n_distinct(query),
    spider_reads = sum(reads),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  right_join(analysis_sample_metadata, by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(number_of_spider_genera, unresolved_spider_asvs,
        number_of_spider_asvs, spider_reads),
      ~coalesce(.x, 0)
    ),
    spider_genus_list = coalesce(
      spider_genus_list,
      "No retained spider detection"
    ),
    sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = rev(spider_web_order))
  ) %>%
  arrange(match(as.character(sample_id), spider_web_order))

```

##### Total spider detection

All retained spider (Order Araneae) records are included, even when genus, family or species is unresolved. The left panel counts distinct spider ASVs; the right panel shows spider reads as a percentage of all retained reads in the same web. Potential host-spider DNA is included. These measures do not estimate the number or proportion of spider individuals.

```{r hs_spider_detection_overview, fig.width=15, fig.height=max(8, 4 + 0.23 * nrow(community_matrix) + 0.12 * length(host_levels))}
# ============================================================
# OVERVIEW: ALL SPIDER DETECTIONS IN EACH WEB SAMPLE
# ============================================================
#
# Each row is one retained web. Include every positive-read Araneae
# record, even when Genus, Family or Species cannot be assigned.
# The left panel counts distinct spider ASVs. The right panel shows
# spider reads as a percentage of all retained reads in that web.
# Both measures use the existing final analysis dataset; no new QC
# filters or changes to the community matrix are introduced.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE PER-WEB READ DENOMINATORS AND SPIDER READ PERCENTAGES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
spider_overview_totals <- mco_HS_plot_data %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_retained_reads = sum(reads),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# The existing spider summary already retains every web, including
# zeros, and counts all spider ASVs regardless of assignment rank.
spider_overview_data <- spider_web_summary %>%
  select(
    sample_id, tentative_species_id,
    number_of_spider_asvs, spider_reads
  ) %>%
  left_join(spider_overview_totals, by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(
    spider_read_percent = if_else(
      total_retained_reads > 0,
      100 * spider_reads / total_retained_reads,
      NA_real_
    ),
    sample_id = factor(
      as.character(sample_id), levels = rev(spider_web_order)
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# KEEP COUNT AND PERCENTAGE IN SEPARATE, CLEARLY LABELED PANELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
spider_overview_plot_data <- spider_overview_data %>%
  select(
    sample_id, tentative_species_id,
    number_of_spider_asvs, spider_read_percent
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(number_of_spider_asvs, spider_read_percent),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    overview_label = case_when(
      metric == "number_of_spider_asvs" ~ as.character(as.integer(value)),
      value > 0 & value < 0.01 ~ "<0.01%",
      TRUE ~ paste0(formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 2), "%")
    ),
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c("number_of_spider_asvs", "spider_read_percent"),
      labels = c(
        "Spider ASVs (count)",
        "Spider reads (% of retained reads)"
      )
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW ONE OVERVIEW FIGURE WITH THE EXISTING HOST AND WEB ORDER
# ------------------------------------------------------------
spider_detection_overview_plot <- ggplot(
  spider_overview_plot_data,
  aes(x = value, y = sample_id)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#257C9D", width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = overview_label), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.8) +
  facet_grid(
    tentative_species_id ~ metric,
    scales = "free",
    space = "free_y",
    switch = "y",
    labeller = labeller(
      tentative_species_id = as_labeller(host_labels)
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.20))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Total spider detection in individual web samples",
    subtitle = "All retained Araneae records; samples grouped by metadata host",
    x = "Count or percentage, as labeled above",
    y = "Web sample",
    caption = paste(
      "Includes spider records unresolved to genus, family or species. Percentages use all retained reads in each web.",
      "Potential host DNA is included. ASV counts and read percentages do not estimate spider individuals or species.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.18, "cm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

spider_detection_overview_plot
```

##### Host-genus-matching spider signal

This figure compares each host spider's metadata genus with genus-level assignments among retained spider ASVs in its own web. A match requires the existing 95% genus identity threshold. Family- or order-only records cannot be resolved as host matches and are excluded from the matching numerator. A genus match is compatible with host DNA, but does not confirm the same species or individual.

```{r hs_host_genus_matching_spider, fig.width=18, fig.height=max(8, 4 + 0.23 * nrow(community_matrix) + 0.12 * length(host_levels))}
# ============================================================
# HOST-GENUS-MATCHING SPIDER SIGNAL IN EACH WEB SAMPLE
# ============================================================
#
# Extract the host genus from the metadata label, then compare it
# with retained spider Genus assignments at the existing 95% identity
# threshold. This is a conservative genus-level match: spider records
# resolved only to Family or Order are not counted as host matches.
#
# Report three complementary quantities for each web:
#   1. Number of host-genus-matching spider ASVs.
#   2. Matching reads as a percentage of all retained reads.
#   3. Matching reads as a percentage of all spider reads.
# These are sequencing signals, not organism abundance or biomass.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# EXTRACT ONE HOST GENUS FOR EVERY RETAINED WEB
# ------------------------------------------------------------
host_genus_key <- analysis_sample_metadata %>%
  transmute(
    sample_id,
    tentative_species_id,
    host_genus = str_extract(
      str_squish(as.character(tentative_species_id)),
      "^[[:alpha:]-]+"
    )
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# IDENTIFY SPIDER ASVs WHOSE GENUS MATCHES THE HOST GENUS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
host_genus_match_by_web <- spider_web_detections %>%
  select(sample_id, query, reads, spider_genus, Best_Identity) %>%
  left_join(
    host_genus_key %>% select(sample_id, host_genus),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    host_genus_match =
      !is.na(host_genus) &
      !is.na(spider_genus) &
      str_to_lower(spider_genus) == str_to_lower(host_genus)
  ) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    host_matching_asvs = n_distinct(query[host_genus_match]),
    host_matching_reads = sum(reads[host_genus_match], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE BOTH READ PERCENTAGES AND RETAIN ZERO-DETECTION WEBS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
host_genus_match_data <- host_genus_key %>%
  left_join(host_genus_match_by_web, by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(
    spider_overview_data %>%
      transmute(
        sample_id = as.character(sample_id),
        total_retained_reads,
        all_spider_reads = spider_reads
      ),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    host_matching_asvs = coalesce(host_matching_asvs, 0L),
    host_matching_reads = coalesce(host_matching_reads, 0),
    host_match_percent_of_retained_reads = if_else(
      total_retained_reads > 0,
      100 * host_matching_reads / total_retained_reads,
      NA_real_
    ),
    host_match_percent_of_spider_reads = if_else(
      all_spider_reads > 0,
      100 * host_matching_reads / all_spider_reads,
      NA_real_
    ),
    sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = rev(spider_web_order))
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PLACE COUNT AND PERCENTAGES IN THREE LABELED PANELS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
host_genus_match_plot_data <- host_genus_match_data %>%
  select(
    sample_id, tentative_species_id, host_genus,
    host_matching_asvs,
    host_match_percent_of_retained_reads,
    host_match_percent_of_spider_reads
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      host_matching_asvs,
      host_match_percent_of_retained_reads,
      host_match_percent_of_spider_reads
    ),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    plot_value = coalesce(value, 0),
    host_match_label = case_when(
      metric == "host_matching_asvs" ~
        as.character(as.integer(value)),
      metric == "host_match_percent_of_spider_reads" & is.na(value) ~
        "No spider reads",
      is.na(value) ~ "NA",
      value > 0 & value < 0.01 ~ "<0.01%",
      TRUE ~ paste0(formatC(value, format = "f", digits = 2), "%")
    ),
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c(
        "host_matching_asvs",
        "host_match_percent_of_retained_reads",
        "host_match_percent_of_spider_reads"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Host-genus-matching spider ASVs (count)",
        "Host-genus-matching reads (% of retained reads)",
        "Host-genus-matching reads (% of spider reads)"
      )
    )
  )

host_genus_match_plot <- ggplot(
  host_genus_match_plot_data,
  aes(x = plot_value, y = sample_id)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#257C9D", width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = host_match_label), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.8) +
  facet_grid(
    tentative_species_id ~ metric,
    scales = "free",
    space = "free_y",
    switch = "y",
    labeller = labeller(
      tentative_species_id = as_labeller(host_labels)
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Host-genus-matching spider signal in individual web samples",
    subtitle = "Conservative genus-level comparison between host metadata and retained spider ASVs",
    x = "Count or percentage, as labeled above",
    y = "Web sample",
    caption = paste(
      "A match requires the detected spider genus to equal the metadata host genus at the existing 95% identity threshold.",
      "Family- and order-level records are excluded from the matching numerator, so unresolved host DNA may be missed.",
      "A genus match is compatible with host DNA but does not confirm the same species or individual.",
      "Read percentages describe sequencing signal, not organism abundance or biomass; no spider reads gives an undefined within-spider percentage.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.18, "cm"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

host_genus_match_plot
```

##### Detailed spider detections

The table and heatmap show assignment labels at their available identification level. Each ASV contributes to one label, but biological classification ranges can overlap: for example, an Araneidae family-level record could belong to Cyclosa. The labels must therefore not be summed as distinct species or as richness at a single taxonomic rank. Heatmap columns are separated by identification rank; blue indicates retained positive reads, rather than abundance.

```{r hs_spider_detailed_detection_table, results='asis'}
if (nrow(spider_web_taxa) > 0) {
  print(knitr::kable(
    spider_web_taxa %>%
      arrange(
        match(sample_id, spider_web_order),
        match(spider_assignment_rank, c("Species", "Genus", "Family", "Order")),
        spider_taxon
      ) %>%
      select(
        sample_id, spider_taxon, spider_assignment_rank,
        spider_family, spider_asvs, spider_reads
      ),
    row.names = FALSE,
    col.names = c(
      "Web sample", "Spider assignment label", "Assignment rank",
      "Family", "Detected ASVs", "Retained reads"
    ),
    caption = paste(
      "Complete spider detection list with sequencing support for each web.",
      "Each ASV contributes to one assignment label; labels at different ranks may cover overlapping biological groups.",
      "Potential host-spider DNA is included. ASV and read counts do not estimate species or individual spider numbers."
    )
  ))
  cat("\n\n")
} else {
  cat("No positive-read Araneae records remain in the final web-analysis table.\n\n")
}
```

```{r hs_spider_detection_heatmap, fig.width=14, fig.height=max(8, 5 + 0.23 * nrow(community_matrix) + 0.12 * length(host_levels))}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 7F: SPIDER ASSIGNMENT LABELS IN INDIVIDUAL WEB SAMPLES
# ============================================================
#
# Each colored cell marks a positive-read spider detection in one web.
# Separate identification ranks visually while retaining every label.
# Each ASV contributes once, but higher-rank labels can contain taxa
# represented in lower-rank columns; columns are not species counts.
# Show all labels in blocks of 20 for readable column labels;
# this is display pagination, not another taxonomic or read filter.

spider_taxon_order <- spider_web_taxa %>%
  group_by(spider_taxon, spider_assignment_rank) %>%
  summarise(detected_webs = n_distinct(sample_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(
    match(spider_assignment_rank, c("Species", "Genus", "Family", "Order")),
    desc(detected_webs),
    spider_taxon
  ) %>%
  pull(spider_taxon)

# Map each existing label to its assignment rank without altering detections.
spider_taxon_rank_key <- spider_web_taxa %>%
  distinct(spider_taxon, spider_assignment_rank)

spider_taxon_blocks <- split(
  seq_along(spider_taxon_order),
  ceiling(seq_along(spider_taxon_order) / 20)
)

for (spider_indices in spider_taxon_blocks) {
  spider_taxa_here <- spider_taxon_order[spider_indices]

  # Rank headers count assignment labels on this page, not spider species.
  spider_rank_counts_here <- spider_taxon_rank_key %>%
    filter(spider_taxon %in% spider_taxa_here) %>%
    count(spider_assignment_rank, name = "assignment_labels")

  spider_rank_labels <- setNames(
    paste0(
      spider_rank_counts_here$spider_assignment_rank, "\n",
      spider_rank_counts_here$assignment_labels,
      ifelse(spider_rank_counts_here$assignment_labels == 1, " label", " labels")
    ),
    spider_rank_counts_here$spider_assignment_rank
  )

  spider_heatmap_data <- expand_grid(
    sample_id = spider_web_order,
    spider_taxon = spider_taxa_here
  ) %>%
    left_join(
      spider_web_taxa %>% select(sample_id, spider_taxon, spider_reads),
      by = c("sample_id", "spider_taxon")
    ) %>%
    left_join(spider_taxon_rank_key, by = "spider_taxon") %>%
    left_join(analysis_sample_metadata, by = "sample_id") %>%
    mutate(
      spider_detection = factor(
        ifelse(coalesce(spider_reads, 0) > 0, "Detected", "Not detected"),
        levels = c("Not detected", "Detected")
      ),
      sample_id = factor(sample_id, levels = rev(spider_web_order)),
      spider_taxon = factor(spider_taxon, levels = spider_taxa_here),
      spider_assignment_rank = factor(
        spider_assignment_rank,
        levels = c("Species", "Genus", "Family", "Order")
      )
    )

  spider_detection_heatmap <- ggplot(
    spider_heatmap_data,
    aes(x = spider_taxon, y = sample_id, fill = spider_detection)
  ) +
    geom_tile(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.2) +
    facet_grid(
      tentative_species_id ~ spider_assignment_rank,
      scales = "free",
      space = "free",
      switch = "y",
      labeller = labeller(
        tentative_species_id = as_labeller(host_labels),
        spider_assignment_rank = as_labeller(spider_rank_labels)
      )
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Not detected" = "#FAFAFA", "Detected" = "#257C9D"),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Spider assignment labels detected in individual web samples",
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Labels ", min(spider_indices), "-", max(spider_indices),
        " of ", length(spider_taxon_order), "; columns grouped by identification rank"
      ),
      x = "Spider assignment label (not a species count)",
      y = "Web sample",
      fill = "Detection",
      caption = paste(
        "Columns are assignment labels at different ranks; they are not a species count or richness at one common rank.",
        "Each ASV contributes once; a higher-rank label can include taxa shown in lower-rank columns.",
        "Blue indicates retained positive reads, not abundance. Potential host DNA is included.",
        "Nondetection is not proof of biological absence.",
        sep = "\n"
      )
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      strip.placement = "outside",
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      strip.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
      panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.18, "cm"),
      panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(0.28, "cm"),
      plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
    )

  print(spider_detection_heatmap)
}
```


##### Host groups and detected spider taxonomy

Read the plot from left to right: host groups from the sample metadata, then the detected spiders' family and genus. A species column is added only when at least one retained detection has a species-level assignment. All detections belong to the spider order Araneae, so this shared rank is omitted. Band width represents retained reads.

Each displayed taxon, unresolved category and host label has its own color. Child nodes do not inherit their parent's color: every branch changes to its destination's color. Unresolved categories are labeled explicitly and are not additional named genera or species. Host labels are separate metadata categories: for example, *Cyclosa conica* and *Cyclosa sp.* remain distinct.

Reads from different hosts merge at the family nodes. Hover over a band or node to highlight all complete host-to-taxon routes that contain it; other routes remain visible. Shared bands keep their pooled widths, even when only some of their reads belong to the selected route. Band tooltips show read counts and the exact contributions from each host group. Counts are not normalized for web number or sequencing depth. Potential host DNA and unresolved assignments are included; reads do not measure spider abundance, biomass, or predation.

```{r hs_spider_read_sankey}
# Use ASV-level taxonomy so family -> genus -> species relationships survive.
# The existing identity thresholds and retained reads are unchanged.
spider_sankey_data <- spider_web_detections %>%
  select(sample_id, reads, spider_family, spider_genus, spider_species,
         spider_assignment_rank) %>%
  left_join(
    analysis_sample_metadata %>% select(sample_id, tentative_species_id),
    by = "sample_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(host = coalesce(as.character(tentative_species_id), "Unassigned host"))

if (nrow(spider_sankey_data) == 0) {
  cat("No retained spider reads are available for the Sankey plot.\n")
} else {
  # A synthetic label such as "Cyclosa sp" is NOT a species identification.
  spider_sankey_has_species <- any(
    spider_sankey_data$spider_assignment_rank == "Species"
  )

  # IDs include the parent lineage, preventing unrelated unresolved groups
  # from being merged. Readable labels and internal IDs have different jobs.
  spider_sankey_paths <- spider_sankey_data %>% mutate(
    host_id = paste0("host::", host),
    family_name = coalesce(spider_family, "Family unresolved (Araneae)"),
    family_id = paste0("family::", family_name),
    genus_name = if_else(
      !is.na(spider_genus), spider_genus,
      paste0("Genus unresolved (", coalesce(spider_family, "Araneae"), ")")
    ),
    genus_id = paste("genus", family_id, genus_name, sep = "::"),
    species_name = if_else(
      spider_assignment_rank == "Species", spider_species,
      paste0("Species unresolved (",
             coalesce(spider_genus, spider_family, "Araneae"), ")")
    ),
    species_id = paste("species", genus_id, species_name, sep = "::")
  )

  # Record complete routes BEFORE pooling adjacent bands. These IDs let
  # hover follow real host -> family -> genus -> species combinations.
  # Merely following every connected band would invent routes after a merge.
  spider_sankey_routes <- spider_sankey_paths %>%
    distinct(host_id, family_id, genus_id, species_id) %>%
    mutate(path_id = row_number())
  spider_sankey_paths <- spider_sankey_paths %>% left_join(
    spider_sankey_routes,
    by = c("host_id", "family_id", "genus_id", "species_id")
  )

  # n includes all retained webs in a host group, even those without spiders.
  spider_sankey_hosts <- analysis_sample_metadata %>%
    mutate(host = coalesce(as.character(tentative_species_id), "Unassigned host")) %>%
    count(host, name = "webs") %>%
    semi_join(spider_sankey_paths, by = "host") %>%
    arrange(match(host, host_levels))

  spider_sankey_nodes <- bind_rows(
    spider_sankey_hosts %>% transmute(
      id = paste0("host::", host), name = paste0(host, " (n=", webs, ")"),
      colour_key = id, stage = 0L
    ),
    spider_sankey_paths %>% distinct(family_id, family_name) %>%
      arrange(family_name) %>% transmute(
        id = family_id, name = family_name, colour_key = family_id, stage = 1L
      ),
    spider_sankey_paths %>% distinct(family_id, genus_id, genus_name) %>%
      arrange(family_id, genus_name) %>% transmute(
        id = genus_id, name = genus_name, colour_key = genus_id, stage = 2L
      )
  )
  if (spider_sankey_has_species) {
    spider_sankey_nodes <- bind_rows(
      spider_sankey_nodes,
      spider_sankey_paths %>%
        distinct(genus_id, species_id, species_name) %>%
        arrange(genus_id, species_name) %>% transmute(
          id = species_id, name = species_name,
          colour_key = species_id, stage = 3L
        )
    )
  }

  # Every node has its own color, including unresolved categories.
  # networkD3 shortens group strings at spaces. Give the color scale safe
  # machine IDs (colour_001, etc.), while keeping full scientific labels.
  spider_sankey_colour_keys <- unique(spider_sankey_nodes$colour_key)
  spider_sankey_nodes <- spider_sankey_nodes %>% mutate(
    group = sprintf("colour_%03d", match(colour_key, spider_sankey_colour_keys))
  ) %>% as.data.frame()
  # Deeper qualitative colors stay visible on a white background.
  # Every category, including unresolved nodes, keeps a distinct color.
  spider_sankey_palette <- c(
    "#0030B0", "#A05050", "#203000", "#906090", "#602000",
    "#5070A0", "#500040", "#202050", "#F000A0", "#501020",
    "#B85C00", "#595959", "#007C91", "#697800", "#A5227A",
    "#00754A", "#8F6500", "#005BBB", "#642A91", "#C6322B",
    "#008000", "#FF0010", "#9050F0", "#706030", "#C010D0",
    "#0050FF", "#880D3F", "#F00060", "#105000", "#3000A0"
  )
  if (length(spider_sankey_colour_keys) > length(spider_sankey_palette)) {
    spider_sankey_palette <- grDevices::hcl.colors(
      length(spider_sankey_colour_keys), palette = "Dynamic"
    )
  }
  spider_sankey_colors <- setNames(
    spider_sankey_palette[seq_along(spider_sankey_colour_keys)],
    sprintf("colour_%03d", seq_along(spider_sankey_colour_keys))
  )
  # Use neutral gray for the family-unresolved node only. Its downstream
  # unresolved-genus category still receives its own distinct color.
  spider_sankey_unknown <- match(
    "family::Family unresolved (Araneae)", spider_sankey_colour_keys
  )
  if (!is.na(spider_sankey_unknown)) {
    spider_sankey_colors[spider_sankey_unknown] <- "#595959"
  }

  # Build each adjacent step from the SAME reads, preserving their lineage.
  spider_sankey_steps <- bind_rows(
    spider_sankey_paths %>% transmute(
      source_id = host_id, target_id = family_id, host, path_id, value = reads
    ),
    spider_sankey_paths %>% transmute(
      source_id = family_id, target_id = genus_id, host, path_id, value = reads
    )
  )
  if (spider_sankey_has_species) {
    spider_sankey_steps <- bind_rows(
      spider_sankey_steps,
      spider_sankey_paths %>% transmute(
        source_id = genus_id, target_id = species_id, host, path_id, value = reads
      )
    )
  }
  spider_sankey_links <- spider_sankey_steps %>%
    group_by(source_id, target_id, host) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(value), path_ids = list(sort(unique(path_id))),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(source_id, target_id, desc(value), host) %>%
    group_by(source_id, target_id) %>%
    summarise(
      path_ids = list(sort(unique(unlist(path_ids)))),
      host_breakdown = paste0(
        host, ": ", format(value, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
        collapse = "\n"
      ),
      value = sum(value), .groups = "drop"
    ) %>% mutate(
      # R indices start at 1; networkD3 indices start at 0.
      source = match(source_id, spider_sankey_nodes$id) - 1L,
      target = match(target_id, spider_sankey_nodes$id) - 1L,
      group = spider_sankey_nodes$group[target + 1L],
      tooltip = paste0(
        spider_sankey_nodes$name[source + 1L], " -> ",
        spider_sankey_nodes$name[target + 1L], "\n",
        format(value, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE),
        " retained reads\n\nHost contributions:\n", host_breakdown
      )
    ) %>% as.data.frame()

  # Store the complete-route IDs touching each node as well as each band.
  spider_sankey_nodes$path_ids <- lapply(spider_sankey_nodes$id, function(id) {
    sort(unique(spider_sankey_steps$path_id[
      spider_sankey_steps$source_id == id | spider_sankey_steps$target_id == id
    ]))
  })

  # Every column transition must account for all retained spider reads.
  # Do not sum values over ALL transitions: that would count reads repeatedly.
  spider_sankey_transition_totals <- tapply(
    spider_sankey_links$value,
    spider_sankey_nodes$stage[spider_sankey_links$source + 1L], sum
  )
  stopifnot(
    !anyNA(spider_sankey_links$source), !anyNA(spider_sankey_links$target),
    !anyDuplicated(spider_sankey_nodes$id),
    all(spider_sankey_transition_totals == sum(spider_sankey_data$reads))
  )

  # Opacity is controlled here in R: 0 = transparent, 1 = fully opaque.
  # Other routes remain visible while a complete route is highlighted.
  spider_sankey_opacity <- list(normal = 0.88, highlight = 1.00, other = 0.45)

  spider_read_sankey <- networkD3::sankeyNetwork(
    Links = spider_sankey_links, Nodes = spider_sankey_nodes,
    Source = "source", Target = "target", Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
    NodeGroup = "group", LinkGroup = "group", units = "retained reads",
    colourScale = htmlwidgets::JS(paste0(
      "d3.scaleOrdinal().domain(", jsonlite::toJSON(names(spider_sankey_colors)),
      ").range(", jsonlite::toJSON(unname(spider_sankey_colors)), ")"
    )),
    fontSize = 13, fontFamily = "Arial", nodeWidth = 22, nodePadding = 22,
    height = max(820, 48 * max(table(spider_sankey_nodes$stage))),
    margin = list(top = 48, right = 12, bottom = 15, left = 12),
    iterations = 64, sinksRight = TRUE
  )
  # Keep extra information on the actual D3 objects, so tooltip matching
  # stays correct even when the browser sorts links by their thickness.
  spider_read_sankey$x$nodes$stage <- spider_sankey_nodes$stage
  spider_read_sankey$x$nodes$path_ids <- spider_sankey_nodes$path_ids
  spider_read_sankey$x$links$tooltip <- spider_sankey_links$tooltip
  spider_read_sankey$x$links$path_ids <- spider_sankey_links$path_ids

  # R supplies the data and color mapping; this small JavaScript callback
  # handles browser-only behavior: hover, readable labels and column titles.
  spider_read_sankey <- htmlwidgets::onRender(
    spider_read_sankey,
    "function(el, x, data) {
      var svg = d3.select(el).select('svg');
      var nodes = svg.selectAll('.node');
      var links = svg.selectAll('.link');

      // A band can contain several complete routes. Match their saved IDs
      // across all columns, without spreading into unrelated sibling routes.
      function pathIds(d) {
        return Array.isArray(d.path_ids) ? d.path_ids : [d.path_ids];
      }
      function highlightRoutes(d) {
        var selected = new Set(pathIds(d));
        function belongsToRoute(item) {
          return pathIds(item).some(function(id) { return selected.has(id); });
        }
        links.style('stroke-opacity', function(l) {
          return belongsToRoute(l) ? data.opacity.highlight : data.opacity.other;
        });
        nodes.select('text').style('font-weight', function(n) {
          return belongsToRoute(n) ? 'bold' : 'normal';
        });
      }
      function resetHighlight() {
        links.style('stroke-opacity', data.opacity.normal);
        nodes.select('text').style('font-weight', 'normal');
      }
      nodes.select('rect').style('opacity', 1).style('fill-opacity', 1)
        .style('stroke-width', 1.2)
        .select('title').text(function(d) {
          return d.name + '\\n' + d3.format(',')(d.value) + ' retained reads';
        });
      nodes.select('text')
        .attr('x', function(d) { return d.stage === data.headings.length - 1 ? -6 : d.dx + 6; })
        .attr('text-anchor', function(d) { return d.stage === data.headings.length - 1 ? 'end' : 'start'; })
        .style('fill', '#111111')
        .style('paint-order', 'stroke')
        .style('stroke', 'white').style('stroke-width', '3px')
        .style('stroke-linejoin', 'round');
      links.each(function(d) {
        d3.select(this).select('title').text(d.tooltip);
      }).style('stroke-opacity', data.opacity.normal)
        .on('mouseover', highlightRoutes)
        .on('mouseout', resetHighlight);
      // Replace native hover handlers for both bands and nodes.
      nodes.on('mouseover', highlightRoutes).on('mouseout', resetHighlight);
      svg.selectAll('.taxonomy-heading').remove();
      data.headings.forEach(function(label, stage) {
        var first = null;
        nodes.each(function(d) {
          if (d.stage === stage && first === null) first = d;
        });
        if (first === null) return;
        svg.append('text').attr('class', 'taxonomy-heading')
          .attr('x', first.x + x.options.margin.left +
            (stage === data.headings.length - 1 ? first.dx : 0))
          .attr('y', 21)
          .attr('text-anchor', stage === data.headings.length - 1 ? 'end' : 'start')
          .style('font-family', 'Arial').style('font-size', '14px')
          .style('font-weight', 'bold').style('fill', '#202020').text(label);
      });
    }",
    data = list(
      headings = c("Host groups (n = webs)", "Family", "Genus",
                   if (spider_sankey_has_species) "Species"),
      opacity = spider_sankey_opacity
    )
  )
  spider_read_sankey <- htmlwidgets::prependContent(
    spider_read_sankey,
    htmltools::tags$p(paste0(
      format(sum(spider_sankey_data$reads), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
      " retained spider reads; ", n_distinct(spider_sankey_data$sample_id),
      " of ", nrow(analysis_sample_metadata), " retained webs have spider detections.",
      if (!spider_sankey_has_species)
        " No species-level assignments pass the current filters; the plot ends at genus."
      else ""
    ))
  )
  spider_read_sankey
}
```


### D. Beta diversity

```{r hs_nmds, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 8: NMDS OF WEB-COMMUNITY COMPOSITION
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: community-composition differences.
#
# The existing method is retained: sample-relative ASV reads,
# Bray-Curtis dissimilarity and a two-dimensional NMDS. Each point
# is a web sample. Nearby points represent more similar
# compositions, approximately; inspect stress and convergence before
# interpreting the layout. NMDS axes have no direct biological meaning
# and are not explained-variance percentages. Visual separation is not a
# significance test.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# CALCULATE RELATIVE READS AND BRAY-CURTIS DISTANCES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmds_relative_matrix <- vegan::decostand(
  community_matrix,
  method = "total"
)
bray_curtis_distance <- vegan::vegdist(
  nmds_relative_matrix,
  method = "bray"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FIT THE TWO-DIMENSIONAL NMDS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(analysis_seed)
# Disable automatic half-change scaling for this dataset.
# This changes coordinate scaling, not stress or input dissimilarities.
mco_HS_nmds <- vegan::metaMDS(
  bray_curtis_distance,
  k = 2,
  trymax = nmds_trymax,
  halfchange = FALSE,
  trace = FALSE
)

# A distance matrix is supplied above, so metaMDS cannot apply another
# transformation to the original counts. Print fitting diagnostics once.

# "Species: scores missing" is expected with a distance-matrix input.
# ASV ordination scores are unavailable; this does not indicate lost data.

mco_HS_nmds

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# EXTRACT SAMPLE COORDINATES AND ATTACH HOST GROUPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmds_scores <- vegan::scores(mco_HS_nmds, display = "sites") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(analysis_sample_metadata, by = "sample_id")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SELECT GROUPS WITH ENOUGH SAMPLES FOR ELLIPSES
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Ellipses are descriptive and do not test group differences.
# Require at least four samples; this only controls the ellipse layer.
# All samples, including those in sparse groups, remain visible as points.
ellipse_species <- host_sample_counts %>%
  filter(number_of_samples >= 4) %>%
  pull(tentative_species_id)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
nmds_plot <- ggplot(
  nmds_scores,
  aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = tentative_species_id)
) +
  stat_ellipse(
    data = nmds_scores %>%
      filter(tentative_species_id %in% ellipse_species),
    aes(group = tentative_species_id),
    type = "t",
    level = 0.95,
    linewidth = 0.6,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = host_colors,
    breaks = host_levels,
    labels = host_labels
  ) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "NMDS of spider-web community composition",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Relative reads; Bray-Curtis; stress = ",
      round(mco_HS_nmds$stress, 3)
    ),
    x = "NMDS1",
    y = "NMDS2",
    color = "Tentative host species",
    caption = "Descriptive ellipses shown only for groups with at least four samples."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

nmds_plot
```

```{r hs_nmds_diagnostics}
# ============================================================
# NMDS FIT DIAGNOSTICS: TWO VERSUS THREE DIMENSIONS
# ============================================================
#
# Compare the same Bray-Curtis distances in two and three dimensions.
# More dimensions can reduce distortion. A lower 3D stress is not a
# significance test, and the first two axes of a 3D fit are not a
# replacement for the two-dimensional plot above.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FIT THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL DIAGNOSTIC
# ------------------------------------------------------------
set.seed(analysis_seed)
mco_HS_nmds_3d <- vegan::metaMDS(
  bray_curtis_distance,
  k = 3,
  trymax = nmds_trymax,
  trace = FALSE
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SUMMARIZE FIT AND STOPPING INFORMATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Repeating the best solution supports stability across random starts;
# it does not prove that a global optimum was found. The stopping
# reason and iteration count below describe the winning start only.
# Inspect them before changing the per-start iteration limit (maxit).
# Increasing random starts does not guarantee an adequate fit.
nmds_models <- list(
  "2D" = mco_HS_nmds,
  "3D" = mco_HS_nmds_3d
)

nmds_stop_reasons <- c(
  "Iteration limit reached",
  "Stress near zero",
  "Stress nearly unchanged",
  "Gradient scale near zero"
)

nmds_fit_summary <- bind_rows(
  lapply(names(nmds_models), function(dimension) {
    fit <- nmds_models[[dimension]]
    tibble(
      Dimensions = dimension,
      Stress = fit$stress,
      Starts = fit$tries,
      Repeated = if_else(fit$converged > 0, "Yes", "No"),
      Iterations = fit$iters,
      Stop_reason = nmds_stop_reasons[fit$icause]
    )
  })
)

knitr::kable(
  nmds_fit_summary,
  digits = 4,
  col.names = c("Dimensions", "Stress", "Starts", "Best repeated", "Iterations", "Stop reason")
)
```

```{r hs_nmds_shepard, fig.width=13, fig.height=6}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 8A: NMDS SHEPARD DIAGNOSTICS
# ============================================================
#
# The x-axis shows observed Bray-Curtis dissimilarity. The y-axis
# shows distance in the fitted ordination. Scatter around the fitted
# monotone line indicates distortion; inspect this together with stress.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# DRAW THE FIGURE
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# stressplot supplies its own x-axis and y-axis titles. Do not pass
# xlab or ylab again, because duplicate arguments stop knitting.
previous_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(1, 2),
  mar = c(4.5, 4.8, 3.5, 1)
)

for (dimension in names(nmds_models)) {
  vegan::stressplot(
    nmds_models[[dimension]],
    pch = 16,
    p.col = "#257C9D",
    cex = 0.55
  )
  title(main = paste(dimension, "NMDS Shepard plot"))
}

par(previous_par)
```


```{r hs_permanova, results='asis'}
# ============================================================
# OVERALL PERMANOVA: COMMUNITY DIFFERENCES AMONG HOST GROUPS
# ============================================================
#
# Test whether ASV composition is associated with host group using
# sample-relative reads and Bray-Curtis dissimilarity. The test uses
# the original distances, not the two-dimensional NMDS coordinates.
# R2 measures the fraction of distance-based variation associated
# with host group; the permutation p-value assesses the overall test.
#
# Each biological sample, after A/B/C merging, is one independent unit.
# Unrestricted permutations assume independent biological samples.
# Available HS location/date fields are constant. For paired or blocked
# experiments, adapt the permutation design before reusing this test.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SELECT THE APPROVED FORMAL-TEST GROUPS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Use groups with at least two retained samples. Singleton groups remain
# in all descriptive analyses. This is the project's analysis rule;
# the remaining n=2-4 groups still provide limited, exploratory evidence.
eligible_hosts <- host_sample_counts %>%
  filter(number_of_samples >= min_group_samples) %>%
  pull(tentative_species_id) %>%
  as.character()

test_metadata <- analysis_sample_metadata %>%
  filter(tentative_species_id %in% eligible_hosts) %>%
  mutate(
    tentative_species_id = droplevels(tentative_species_id)
  )

can_run_group_tests <- length(eligible_hosts) >= 2
omnibus_p <- NA_real_

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# FIT AND REPORT THE OVERALL MODEL
# ------------------------------------------------------------
if (can_run_group_tests) {

  # Match matrix rows to metadata by ID; keep every ASV column.
  test_relative_matrix <- nmds_relative_matrix[
    test_metadata$sample_id, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  test_bray <- vegan::vegdist(
    test_relative_matrix,
    method = "bray"
  )

  # Reuse these biological-sample permutations for the dispersion test.
  set.seed(analysis_seed)
  test_permutations <- permute::shuffleSet(
    nrow(test_metadata),
    nset = n_permutations,
    control = permute::how(nperm = n_permutations)
  )

  permanova_model <- vegan::adonis2(
    test_bray ~ tentative_species_id,
    data = test_metadata,
    permutations = test_permutations
  )
  omnibus_p <- as.numeric(permanova_model[1, "Pr(>F)"])

  print(knitr::kable(
    as.data.frame(permanova_model),
    digits = 4,
    caption = paste0(
      "Overall PERMANOVA: ", nrow(test_metadata), " samples in ",
      length(eligible_hosts), " host groups; ", nrow(test_permutations),
      " permutations; seed ", analysis_seed, "."
    )
  ))

} else {
  cat("Formal group tests require at least two host groups with repeated samples.\n")
}
```


```{r hs_beta_dispersion, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# ============================================================
# PLOT 9: WITHIN-GROUP BETA DISPERSION
# ============================================================
#
# Main figure: within-group heterogeneity.
#
# This shows distances to each host group's spatial median in the
# principal coordinate space of the Bray-Curtis distances, not
# distances measured on the two-dimensional NMDS plot. Larger values
# indicate greater within-group heterogeneity. Here type = "median", so
# these are distances to spatial medians, not centroids.
# Use the same eligible samples as the overall PERMANOVA, with the
# small-sample bias adjustment. Singleton groups remain descriptive.
# The permutation test asks whether within-group dispersion differs.
# Interpret it alongside PERMANOVA: unequal dispersion can contribute
# to a significant PERMANOVA, especially with unequal group sizes.

if (can_run_group_tests) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # ALIGN HOST LABELS WITH THE DISTANCE MATRIX
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # test_bray was constructed in test_metadata sample-ID order above.
  ordered_nmds_metadata <- test_metadata

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # CALCULATE DISTANCES TO GROUP SPATIAL MEDIANS
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  dispersion_model <- vegan::betadisper(
    test_bray,
    group = ordered_nmds_metadata$tentative_species_id,
    type = "median",
    bias.adjust = TRUE
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # PREPARE THE DISPERSION PLOT TABLE
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  dispersion_plot_data <- tibble(
    sample_id = names(dispersion_model$distances),
    distance_to_median = as.numeric(dispersion_model$distances)
  ) %>%
    left_join(test_metadata, by = "sample_id")

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # DRAW THE FIGURE
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  dispersion_plot <- ggplot(
    dispersion_plot_data,
    aes(x = tentative_species_id, y = distance_to_median)
  ) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "grey90", outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.6) +
    geom_point(
      aes(color = tentative_species_id),
      position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 123),
      size = 2.3,
      alpha = 0.85
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = host_colors,
      breaks = eligible_hosts
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = rev(eligible_hosts),
      labels = host_labels
    ) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(
      title = "Within-group dispersion by host-spider species",
      subtitle = "Bray-Curtis; eligible groups; small-sample bias adjustment",
      x = "Tentative host-spider species",
      y = "Bias-adjusted distance to group spatial median",
      caption = "The plot and permutation test use the same eligible samples; singleton groups remain descriptive."
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()
    )

  print(dispersion_plot)
}
```

```{r hs_dispersion_test, results='asis'}
# ============================================================
# PERMUTATION TEST OF WITHIN-GROUP DISPERSION
# ============================================================
#
# Spatial medians and bias.adjust = TRUE match the preceding plot.
# The adjustment scales distances by sqrt(n / (n - 1)) within each
# group. It reduces small-sample bias but does not overcome low power.
# No square-root or additive correction is applied to Bray-Curtis;
# any distance warnings remain visible for review.

if (can_run_group_tests) {

  dispersion_test <- vegan::permutest(
    dispersion_model,
    permutations = test_permutations,
    pairwise = FALSE
  )

  print(knitr::kable(
    as.data.frame(dispersion_test$tab),
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Permutation test of differences in within-group dispersion."
  ))
}

# A significant dispersion test indicates differences in within-group
# variability. If PERMANOVA is also significant, do not attribute the
# result solely to differences in group location. A nonsignificant
# dispersion result does not prove equality, especially in small groups.
# These tests describe associations, not causal host preferences.
```


```{r hs_pairwise_permanova, results='asis'}
# ============================================================
# CONDITIONAL PAIRWISE PERMANOVA
# ============================================================
#
# Run every pair among the eligible host groups only if the overall
# PERMANOVA p-value is below test_alpha. Use the same relative-read
# Bray-Curtis distances, and adjust p-values by Holm's method across
# the complete set of comparisons. Small groups remain exploratory.

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# PREPARE PERMUTATIONS FOR A TWO-GROUP COMPARISON
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# For two groups, choose(n, n_a) gives the number of unique assignments
# of samples to the first group. Enumerate all assignments when feasible;
# otherwise use the configured number of random permutations.
#
# Rows must be ordered with group A first and group B second. Exclude
# the observed assignment from the permutation matrix because adonis2
# includes the observed statistic when calculating its p-value.
# Reordering samples within a group adds no new test statistic.
# This enumeration assumes unrestricted, independent biological samples.
make_pair_permutations <- function(n, n_a, requested) {

  possible <- choose(n, n_a)

  if (is.finite(possible) && possible <= requested + 1) {

    allocations <- utils::combn(
      seq_len(n),
      n_a,
      simplify = FALSE
    )
    observed <- seq_len(n_a)
    allocations <- Filter(
      function(x) !identical(as.integer(x), observed),
      allocations
    )

    indices <- do.call(
      rbind,
      lapply(allocations, function(x) {
        c(x, setdiff(seq_len(n), x))
      })
    )
    storage.mode(indices) <- "integer"

    return(list(indices = indices, method = "Exact"))
  }

  indices <- permute::shuffleSet(
    n,
    nset = requested,
    control = permute::how(nperm = requested)
  )

  list(indices = indices, method = "Random")
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# RUN THE APPROVED CONDITIONAL COMPARISONS
# ------------------------------------------------------------
run_pairwise <- can_run_group_tests &&
  is.finite(omnibus_p) && omnibus_p < test_alpha

if (run_pairwise) {

  host_pairs <- utils::combn(eligible_hosts, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  full_bray_matrix <- as.matrix(bray_curtis_distance)
  set.seed(analysis_seed)

  pairwise_results <- bind_rows(
    lapply(host_pairs, function(pair) {

      pair_metadata <- test_metadata %>%
        filter(tentative_species_id %in% pair) %>%
        mutate(
          tentative_species_id = factor(
            as.character(tentative_species_id),
            levels = pair
          )
        ) %>%
        arrange(tentative_species_id, sample_id)

      n_a <- sum(pair_metadata$tentative_species_id == pair[1])
      n_b <- sum(pair_metadata$tentative_species_id == pair[2])
      sample_ids <- pair_metadata$sample_id

      pair_bray <- as.dist(
        full_bray_matrix[sample_ids, sample_ids, drop = FALSE]
      )
      pair_permutations <- make_pair_permutations(
        length(sample_ids),
        n_a,
        n_permutations
      )

      pair_model <- vegan::adonis2(
        pair_bray ~ tentative_species_id,
        data = pair_metadata,
        permutations = pair_permutations$indices
      )

      tibble(
        Host_A = pair[1],
        Host_B = pair[2],
        n_A = n_a,
        n_B = n_b,
        R2 = as.numeric(pair_model[1, "R2"]),
        pseudo_F = as.numeric(pair_model[1, "F"]),
        p_raw = as.numeric(pair_model[1, "Pr(>F)"]),
        permutation_rows = nrow(pair_permutations$indices),
        method = pair_permutations$method
      )
    })
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      p_Holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm", n = length(host_pairs))
    ) %>%
    select(
      Host_A, Host_B, n_A, n_B, R2, pseudo_F,
      p_raw, p_Holm, permutation_rows, method
    )

  # Report every eligible pair, not only comparisons with small p-values.
  # Exact p-values can be coarse when only a few assignments are possible.
  print(knitr::kable(
    pairwise_results,
    digits = 4,
    col.names = c(
      "Host A", "Host B", "n A", "n B", "R2", "Pseudo-F",
      "Raw p", "Holm p", "Permutations", "Method"
    ),
    caption = paste0(
      "All ", nrow(pairwise_results),
      " eligible host-pair comparisons; Holm correction across the full set."
    )
  ))

} else if (can_run_group_tests && is.finite(omnibus_p)) {
  cat("Pairwise PERMANOVA was not run because the overall test did not pass the significance threshold.\n")
} else {
  cat("Pairwise PERMANOVA was not run because a valid overall comparison was unavailable.\n")
}

# Read pairwise results together with the overall dispersion test.
# Small and unequal groups limit inference; a significant comparison
# does not establish host preference or explain the biological mechanism.
```
